title: Backend Development Readiness
description: Assess your skills in server architectures, RESTful API design, relational schemas, caching, authentication, and error handling.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code should a REST API return when a resource is successfully created?
options: 200 OK
201 Created
204 No Content
202 Accepted
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a clustered and non-clustered index in relational databases?
options: A clustered index determines the physical order of data rows in a table, so only one can exist per table
Non-clustered indexes cannot be used on foreign keys
Clustered indexes are stored in RAM while non-clustered are on disk
A table can have up to 10 clustered indexes
questions.explanation: A clustered index physically sorts table rows on disk based on the key; hence, only one clustered index can exist per table.

questions.question: What makes an HTTP method idempotent?
options: Multiple identical requests have the exact same side-effect on the server as a single request
The request never alters database state (safe)
The server caches the response forever
It can only be invoked by authenticated administrators
questions.explanation: An HTTP method is idempotent if executing it multiple times produces the same server state as executing it once (e.g., PUT, DELETE, GET).

questions.question: Why should password hashes always use a unique 'salt' along with a slow key-derivation function like bcrypt or Argon2?
options: To prevent precomputed rainbow table attacks and slow down brute-force attempts
To compress the password length to fit into fixed-width VARCHAR columns
To allow password recovery in plain text by administrators
To encrypt database backups in transit
questions.explanation: Salts ensure identical passwords have different hash outputs, mitigating rainbow table lookups; slow algorithms thwart offline GPU cracking.

questions.question: In a JWT (JSON Web Token), which part contains the claims such as user ID and expiration timestamp?
options: Header
Payload
Signature
Secret key
questions.explanation: The payload is the second part of a JWT and contains encoded claims (statements about an entity and additional data).

questions.question: What is the primary role of Redis in high-throughput backend systems?
options: An in-memory key-value data store used for low-latency caching, session management, and rate limiting
A document database for storing unstructured multimedia files
An automated CI/CD deployment runner
A relational database management system with ACID transactions
questions.explanation: Redis operates in RAM, delivering sub-millisecond responses ideal for caching hot data, tracking user sessions, and enforcing rate limits.

questions.question: In database transaction management, what does the 'I' in ACID stand for?
options: Integrity
Isolation
Immutability
Indexing
questions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. Isolation ensures concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other.

questions.question: What is the 'N+1 Query Problem' when using ORMs like SQLAlchemy or Prisma?
options: Executing 1 initial query to get N parent rows, followed by N separate individual queries to fetch child relations
Allocating N+1 database connections in the connection pool
Adding N+1 indexes to a table causing write slowdowns
Executing recursive SQL statements until a condition is met
questions.explanation: The N+1 problem occurs when an application executes 1 query for parent records and then fires N additional queries for related records instead of using a JOIN/eager loading.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an API Gateway in microservices architecture?
options: Acts as a single entry point handling routing, rate limiting, authentication, and SSL termination
Replaces all backend database storage engines
Compiles backend source code to machine assembly
Generates automated mock test datasets
questions.explanation: An API gateway sits between clients and microservices, centralizing cross-cutting concerns like traffic routing, authentication, and throttling.

questions.question: Which database isolation level prevents dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads completely?
options: Read Uncommitted
Read Committed
Repeatable Read
Serializable
questions.explanation: Serializable is the strictest isolation level, ensuring concurrent transaction execution produces the same outcome as if they ran serially.
